rows.evidence: Q1: Application section and Results (Figs 2-3) - the authors run MOBIDIC-WRM daily over 1992-2006 for the Arno basin at 200 m resolution, calibrate on 15 sub-basins (1993-1998) and compare modelled flow duration curves and daily discharge with gauged data; Water budget section and Fig. 5/Table 2 - own computation of residual flow WB = Q - EF - W for 44 sections and classification of sub-basins into four water-deficit classes.
rows.notes: The study is a primary modelling study, but the technology it tests is a distributed hydrological model (MOBIDIC-WRM) calibrated and validated against river gauge data, not remote sensing. Remote sensing appears only as an ancillary data source ('land cover, geology and soil hydraulic properties retrieved from existing maps and from remote sensing data'); the package's capability to use remotely sensed land surface temperature for calibration/validation is described generically but not applied in the Arno case, where calibration used measured flow duration curves. The study does report its own result on identifying critical sub-areas (Fig. 5, Table 2: sub-basins with extreme/severe deficit, concentrated in southern tributaries) and on comparing withdrawals with environmental flow (Q7,2) for June-September, and states that critical levels correspond to government requirements such as constraints on new withdrawal permissions; this supports the passage's effect for the hydrological model, but it does not isolate or evaluate any contribution of remote sensing to that effect. Had the technology matched: triangulation no (single model checked against gauges); representativeness no (one basin); scalability yes (basin/sub-basin scale); limitations partly stated (poor agreement where groundwater needs more detailed representation; simplified groundwater scheme due to data scarcity); no dispersion measure for the deficit classification.

notes: Full text appears complete (IAHS Publ. 327, 2009, pp. 52-61). Figures 2-5 are referenced but images are not reproduced in the text; their captions and the text description were used.
